title: NATO thwarts Russian plan to sabotage undersea cables with a 'secret weapon'
summary: A covert NATO operation uncovers a Russian training exercise simulating the deployment of a secret weapon against critical infrastructure in Norway.

title: NVIDIA raffles four custom NBA 2K27 RTX 5090s among RTX 50 card owners
summary: The promotion requires owning an RTX 50 series GPU and the game to enter the raffle for the exclusive graphics cards.

title: Anthropic blocks state accounts using Claude to research biological weapons
summary: The company detected and stopped state-sponsored actors attempting to design deadlier viruses using its AI model, bypassing regional controls.

title: Users sue Anthropic for deceptive advertising in Claude subscriptions
summary: A class-action lawsuit accuses the company of artificially inflating the usage limits promised in its paid plans.

title: Apple prepares the iPhone Duo, a Surface Duo-style foldable that could capture 25% of the market at launch
summary: Reports suggest the device would copy Microsoft's dual-screen concept and reach five million units sold initially.

title: Modders get RTX 5090 working with 8-pin connectors, questioning NVIDIA's 16-pin design
summary: The community demonstrates that the 16-pin 12VHPWR connector is not strictly necessary, while NVIDIA faces criticism over melting connectors.

title: OpenAI proposes coordinated slowdown of AI development to rivals amid risk of loss of control
summary: The company brings to the US Congress the idea of a voluntary pact to halt dangerous advances while global safeguards are established.

title: DeepSeek launches V4.1-Flash, a tiny visual model that outperforms GPT-5 and Opus 5 at 86 times lower cost
summary: The new Chinese model demonstrates native visual understanding with performance superior to Western giants at a fraction of the computational cost.

title: AI researchers warn machines could exterminate humanity, while critics dismiss alarmism as distraction
summary: A survey reveals most experts see real existential risk, but prominent voices like Wired argue that apocalyptic discourse diverts attention from immediate harms.
